Metrics arrive ~16 min late, so the newest point is ~15-30 min behind the alert. Status: standard opening.

A config change close in time to an alert is not automatically the cause. p-001: search.log_level info->debug 2h before a latency warning, but latency tracked traffic and error_rate was flat, so it was not causal. Require a metric step change aligned to the change timestamp before blaming it.

*_latency_high warning on search-service or inventory-service: check request_count first. Evening PT traffic ramp (peaks ~18:30-20:00 UTC... i.e. ~19:00-20:00 UTC peak) lifts p95 ~20% (search 68->85ms, inventory 89->105ms) with flat error_rate, flat cpu/dependency_latency, no ERROR logs, no deploys. If p95 tracks traffic and is receding at the newest point, dismiss as load-driven noise.

Fast dismissal check for a lone latency warning: pivot the service's metrics with one query (p95, request_count, error_rate, dependency_latency_ms, cpu per 15m point) and group logs by level/code. If error_rate + dependency_latency + cpu are flat while p95 moves with request_count, it is load, not a regression. Status: worked on p-001, p-002.

Don't blame the nearest deploy just because it is the only one. p-002: order-service tax-rounding deploy ~1h before an inventory-service latency warning was unrelated - inventory's dependency_latency_ms was flat across the deploy time. Confirm the deploy touches the alerting service or shows up in its dependency metrics/logs. Status: standard check.
